study_identification_part.si_4_title: Neuroanatomical heterogeneity and homogeneity in individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Person-Based Similarity Index (PBSI) was used to quantify the similarity of an individual's brain profile to a normative (healthy control) reference. PBSI scores were calculated by correlating each CHR-P individual's neuroanatomical profile (SA, CT, SV) with those of healthy controls, then transforming to z-scores. Individuals with >1.5 SD deviation were identified as markedly deviant from the normative profile.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Personalised estimates of heterogeneity of SA, CT and SV brain profiles were indexed with the novel Person-Based Similarity Index (PBSI), with two complementary applications. First, to assess the extent of within-diagnosis similarity or divergence of neuroanatomical profiles between individuals. Second, using a normative modelling approach, to assess the 'normativeness' of neuroanatomical profiles in individuals at CHR-P.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: 68 cortical regions were measured for both Surface Area (SA) and Cortical Thickness (CT) according to the Desikan-Killiany atlas, 16 subcortical volume (SV) variables, and one measure of Intracranial Volume (ICV), totaling 153 structural ROIs. FreeSurfer automated pipelines were used for processing.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: The application of this protocol yielded a total of 153 structural ROIs: 68 cortical variables measured by both Surface Area (SA) and Cortical Thickness (CT) according to the Desikan-Killiany atlas, 16 Subcortical Volume (SV) variables and one measure of Intracranial Volume (ICV).

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Neuroimaging data were harmonized using neuroComBat to adjust for scanner protocol and site effects while controlling for group (CHR-P/HC), age and sex. In PBSI regression analyses, age and sex were included as covariates.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: Neuroimaging data were adjusted for scanner protocol and site using neuroComBat, a batch-adjustment method that relies on an empirical Bayes framework to assess the influence of covariates of interest. The neuroimaging data were adjusted prior to current analyses, as this approach is recommended by the tool developers for optimal use while controlling for group (CHR-P/HC), age and sex.
